title: Completed recording and skip run
statement: Let $k,n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $x$ be a finite Boolean word, let $d$ be a configuration with $k+2$ work tapes, Boolean symbols, and record states, and let $a$ be an action whose successor state is in $\{0,\ldots,n\}$ or absent. Suppose $d$ has the initial recording-machine state and its table tape contains, in order from its current head position, the bits encoding $a$. After one more step than the length of that encoding, the record-and-skip machine has the same input-head position, work-tape contents, output, and all work-tape head positions as $d$, except that the table-tape head has advanced by the encoding length. Its state is the successor phase marked done, with the Boolean value indicating whether $a$ has a successor state.
hypotheses_covered: Configuration d with k+2 tapes and record states
Action a with state in Fin (n+1)
d has the initial recording-machine state
Every encoded action bit occurs in the corresponding table-tape cell
